rocketIntro: Welcome, Flight Director! First, pick the rocket that will carry your crew.
Bigger rockets lift more but cost more. Your capsule has to fit what it can lift.
intro: Now build the capsule. Pick one part from each list on the left.
Watch the margin on the right. Keep the capsule lighter than your rocket can lift.
shell: The shell is the crew's home, like a camper van for space.
Roomier means a happier crew, but every extra tonne has to be lifted.
lifeSupport: Life support makes air, water and warmth for the crew.
Cheap systems break more often. Think of a cheap tent in a storm.
power: The battery is like a phone battery for the whole capsule.
Add up what your parts use. The battery has to cover all of it.
comms: The radio is your phone line to Mission Control.
A better radio means clearer calls and earlier warnings, but it uses more power.
computer: The flight computer is the capsule's brain. It steers and checks every system.
Cheap computers run cheap code. Software bugs have ended real missions.
mass: A rocket can only lift so much, like a car with a roof box.
Keep your capsule lighter than the rocket can lift, with room to spare.
rocket: A rocket is like a moving truck. Each one can only carry so many tonnes.
Proven rockets have flown a lot. Risky ones are new or reused. Pick with care.
site: Where you launch matters, like picking an airport for a big trip.
Some sites are cheap, some give extra lift, and every one has its own weather.
lockIn: Build locked in! Next comes five weeks of building, testing and training.
Measure twice, launch once. Let's get to work.

hal.budgetLifeSupport: Cheap air. I've seen this movie before. It doesn't end well.
hal.budgetComputer: Bargain computer. Bargain code. Bugs love a bargain.
hal.powerTight: Power's tight. You'll run out of juice at the worst moment.
hal.powerOver: Your parts want more power than that battery has. Something goes dark in flight.
hal.premiumBroke: Premium everything. Fancy. Now how do you pay the electric bill?
hal.condorReflown: Reused booster. Fine, if you test it. Do you test it?
hal.pelican: Brand-new rocket. No track record. I don't love that.
hal.kodiak: Cold is hard on rubber seals. Plan for frost.
hal.kourou: Everything arrives late down there. Pad extra days.
hal.mahia: Island pad. Parts come by boat. Slowly.
hal.sriharikota: Monsoon season. Rain, wind, more rain. Watch the sky.
hal.marginThin: No room for surprises. Everything gets heavier during testing.
hal.lockPowerShort: Power is short. Lock this in and something goes dark up there.
